name: OpenCode
works_with: Your terminal, plus a desktop app (beta) for macOS, Windows and Linux
short: An open source AI coding agent for your terminal, with a build agent for changes and a read-only plan agent for exploring code.
what: OpenCode is an open source AI coding agent. It comes with two built-in agents and the `Tab` key switches between them. The default, build, has full access for development work. The other, plan, is read-only: it can't edit files unless you allow it, and it asks before it runs bash commands. A general subagent handles complex searches and multistep tasks, and you can call it with `@general`. There is also a desktop app in beta.
who: Developers who want a coding agent that runs in the terminal and is open source. The plan agent is a good way to look around an unfamiliar codebase before you let anything change it.
needs: One of: npm, bun, pnpm or yarn, Homebrew, pacman or paru on Arch, mise, or Nix. You can also use the install script

steps.title: Install with the script
steps.text: The README calls this the YOLO option. Read the script before you pipe it into bash.

steps.title: Or install with npm
steps.text: bun, pnpm and yarn also work.

steps.title: Or install with Homebrew
steps.text: The README recommends this tap on macOS and Linux because it is always up to date. The official formula, `brew install opencode`, is updated less often.

steps.title: Other package managers
steps.text: On Arch, use `sudo pacman -S opencode` for stable or `paru -S opencode-beta` for the latest from the AUR. On any OS, `mise use -g opencode`. With Nix, `nix run github:anomalyco/opencode`.

steps.title: Remove old versions first
steps.text: The README says to remove any version older than 0.1.x before installing.

steps.title: Or get the desktop app (beta)
steps.text: Download it from opencode.ai/download, or install it on macOS with Homebrew.

steps.title: Switch agents
steps.text: Press `Tab` to move between build and plan. Configuration is covered in the docs at opencode.ai/docs.

try.label: A first prompt
try.where: OpenCode, with the plan agent selected
try.text: Explain how this project is laid out and where I should start reading.

watch: The install script is piped straight into bash. Read it before you run it.
The default build agent has full access to your project. Use plan if you want file edits denied and a prompt before every bash command.
The desktop app is marked beta.
The README doesn't say which AI models it uses or what they cost. Check the docs before you start.
